Allowed hosts are extra Host header values the server accepts (DNS-rebinding guard). localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 and the host parts of addr and public_url are always allowed. A wildcard bind (0.0.0.0, ::) adds no name: to reach onett remotely (e.g. over Tailscale), list the name you use here, or requests get 421 Misdirected Request.

Retain events and RetainRunLogs bound how long the event history and agent run logs are kept; older rows are deleted once a day, so a daemon that runs for months does not grow without limit. Tasks, runs, deployments and approvals are kept. Defaults 720h (30 days) and 2160h (90 days); a very large value (e.g. 876000h) keeps them in practice forever.
Max size is the largest single file accepted, such as "25MB" (default 25MB). A larger upload is refused with 413 and nothing is kept.
Max per message is how many files one message may carry (default 10).
Retention is how long an attachment is kept; older files and their records are deleted once a day, and a message that referenced one shows without it (default 720h = 30 days).

Session idle timeout is how long the agent process of an orchestrator or goal conversation stays alive after its last turn (default 30m). While it lives, each message goes to the same process, so the prompt cache keeps hitting and MCP servers connect once; after it, the next message resumes the session in a new process. A negative value turns the long-lived process off: every turn then starts its own process.

Daily budget usd stops new task runs once today's reported agent cost reaches it (0 = no limit). Only pay-per-token runs count: runs on a flat-rate subscription (see Harness.Billing) report an API-price estimate that nobody is billed for. Chat with the orchestrator is exempt. Codex reports no cost, so it is counted only when its harness has a price.
Max goal turns is how many orchestrator turns one goal gets before it is blocked (default 40).

Run shim starts each agent behind a small per-run helper process (onett run-shim) that owns the agent and its output, so the agent can outlive a restart of onett, which picks the run up again when it comes back. Default true; read it with RunShimOn.

Inherit env names extra variables passed through from onett's own environment. Agents otherwise get only a small allowlist (PATH, HOME, USER, LANG, TERM, TMPDIR, ...), so secrets loaded into onett (GH_TOKEN, provider tokens) do not reach them.
Price lets onett estimate the cost of runs whose harness reports tokens but no dollar cost (codex), so limits.daily_budget_usd counts them.

Billing says how this harness's runs are paid for: "auto" (default; the adapter detects it), "metered" (pay per token) or "subscription" (flat rate). A value other than auto overrides detection for every run. Subscription runs do not count toward limits.daily_budget_usd.

Isolate runs the agent without the owner's personal Claude Code setup (their MCP connectors, plugins, hooks and user-level settings). Default false: agents use the owner's setup. Set true to drop it, for example when connectors that come and go between turns keep breaking the prompt cache. Only claude-code has such a setup; other harness types ignore it. Read it with IsolateOn.

Description is shown in the UI and given to the orchestrator so it can pick roles.

CIGrace: after onett pushes, a PR with no checks yet counts as CI pending (not "no CI") for this long, so a fast review cannot merge before CI registers. Default 3m.
RequireChecks: for repositories that always run CI, a PR with no checks never passes the CI gate (it waits, then blocks after 30m) instead of counting as "no CI configured".
Gates by risk level: "low", "medium", "high".

Checks run in the worktree after the agent finishes and before onett commits and pushes (formatters, linters, fast tests). A failing check fails the attempt: the task is re-queued with the check's output, like a CI failure, without spending a CI run.
Run is a shell command (sh -c) run in the worktree with the agent's environment (the allowlist, the harness's inherit_env, the project's env).
Timeout defaults to 10m.

Setup runs in a fresh worktree before the agent starts (install dependencies, generate code), so the agent can build and test. A failing setup command fails the attempt before the agent runs: the task is re-queued with the command's output. Setup and checks run with the agent's environment, not onett's, because they execute code the agent may have written.
Run is a shell command (sh -c) run in the worktree with the agent's environment (the allowlist, the harness's inherit_env, the project's env).
Timeout defaults to 10m.
Intake sources turn external work queues into tasks: each command prints tasks as JSON lines (see docs/plugins.md, "Intake sources"). Run by the exec_intake loop.
Command is a shell command (sh -c) that prints zero or more tasks, one JSON object per line: {"id","title","body","kind","priority","role"}. id is required and dedupes.
Kind is the default task kind when a line has none (default "feature").
Timeout for one run of Command (default 60s).
Deploy is the shell command that releases the commit in ONETT_REF. Its last output line may be a JSON object {"id","url","state"} or a bare URL. Required.
Status is the shell command that reports a release's state, given ONETT_DEPLOY_ID. Default: none; a deploy is then treated as finished as soon as the deploy command exits.
Rollback is the shell command that restores an earlier release. Default: none, so a rollback cannot be done.
Timeout limits each of the three commands. Default 30m.
Health url must answer 2xx during the verify window. Empty skips the HTTP check.
Logs is a shell command that prints the service's recent logs (e.g. "tail -n 200 /var/log/app.log", "vercel logs <url>"). Its output tail is attached to incidents.
Verify for is how long a release is watched before it is called healthy. Default 10m.
Timeout fails a release still building after this long. Default 30m.
Auto rollback rolls back on a failed verify window. Default true.
Command is the shell command that prints the production signals it sees, as a JSON array or JSON Lines. It receives ONETT_SINCE (RFC 3339). Required.
Timeout limits one run of the command. Default 60s.
Org is the Sentry organization slug. Required.
Project is the Sentry project slug. Required.
Base url is the Sentry server URL. Default https://sentry.io.
Token env is the name of an environment variable that holds the Sentry API token. Default SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN.
Query is the Sentry issue search to run. Default is:unresolved.

Retro periodically gives an improver agent the evidence of what went wrong recently (blocked/failed tasks and their reasons, open friction, incidents, review findings) to fix the top problem, consolidate duplicate friction issues and file follow-ups. Default every 24h; enabled by default only for self_project (it spends agent time).

Goals wakes the orchestrator on each active goal whose last step has settled. Default every 1m.

Heartbeat wakes the orchestrator on a schedule when the attention digest (blocked or failed work, stuck queues, failed deploys, pending approvals) has an item it has not shown before. Default every 15m.
Quiet hours is a window such as "22:00-07:00", in the daemon's local time, when the heartbeat does not wake anyone. It may wrap midnight. Empty means no quiet hours.
Stale queued is how long a task may sit queued before it counts as stuck; default 4h.

Webhook url env is the name of an environment variable that holds the Discord webhook URL, which contains a secret token. Required.
Username overrides the webhook's display name. Default: the name set in Discord.
Command is the shell command run for each notification. It receives ONETT_NOTIFY_TITLE, ONETT_NOTIFY_BODY, ONETT_NOTIFY_PRIORITY and ONETT_NOTIFY_URL in its environment. Required.
Server is the ntfy server URL. Default https://ntfy.sh.
Topic is the ntfy topic to publish to. Required.
Token env is the name of an environment variable that holds an ntfy access token, sent as a Bearer token. Optional; without it the notifier posts anonymously.
Bot token env is the name of an environment variable that holds the Telegram bot token. Required.
Chat id is the chat to send to: a numeric ID or @channelname. Required.
Api url is the Telegram Bot API base URL. Default https://api.telegram.org.
Skip approvals drops approval requests, for use beside a two-way Telegram channel that already carries them. Default false.
